Team Lorraine Mulligan of RE/MAX Results award-winning international RE/MAX agents for over 25 years is delighted to welcome you to this beautifully presented three-bedroom, mid-terrace ground-floor duplex, rated BER B1 for outstanding energy efficiency.

Don`t be fooled by first impressions: this home is far more spacious than it appears from the outside, offering genuinely luxurious and comfortable living across two floors. As a mid-terrace property, it also benefits from superior warmth and security compared to end-of-terrace or detached alternatives.

The current owners, a professional couple, have invested more than 50,000 in thoughtful upgrades, and it shows the home is presented in pristine, move-in-ready condition throughout. Outside, you`ll find communal parking and a sunny, south-facing rear garden with a low-maintenance tiled patio, perfect for relaxed evenings or entertaining.

Whether you`re a first-time buyer, looking to trade down to something more manageable and economical to run, or an investor seeking strong rental potential, this property ticks every box.

Its location is just as compelling. Adamstown offers a genuinely rare mix of convenience and community: local schools, GAA and athletics clubs, parks and a newly built community centre with regular family activities are all within easy reach, along with a playground for younger children. The train station is a 10-minute walk and puts you in Heuston Station in just 12 minutes, while the picturesque village of Lucan is a pleasant 20-minute stroll away. Frequent 25, 25A and 25B bus services (every 10 15 minutes) connect you directly to Dublin city centre in around 30 minutes.

There is also a newly built community centre close by, which holds activities and events for families. The train station is an approx. 10-minute walk in one direction and can have you in Heuston Station in 12 minutes. The beautiful Lucan village is an approx. 20-minute walk in the other direction. Adamstown is a prime location for bus routes as you have the 25, 25A and 25B which provide a service every 10 to 15 minutes that will take you straight into Dublin city centre in around 30 minutes. In Adamstown there is also a small playground within walking distance from the property for young children. 

Accommodation briefly comprises of a kitchen/dining room, sitting room, guest W.C., 3 bedrooms (master ensuite) and a bathroom.

INFORMATION ABOUT ADAMSTOWN, LUCAN, CO. DUBLIN.
In 2024, Adamstown in Lucan, Co. Dublin, is a rapidly growing area supported by a well-planned range of facilities and infrastructure. As part of the South Dublin County Council`s Strategic Development Zone (SDZ), Adamstown is designed to offer a balanced mix of residential, commercial, educational, and recreational amenities.

Transportation and Accessibility: Adamstown benefits from the Kildare rail line with a local station that connects to Dublin city and beyond. Plans are also in place to extend the Luas Red Line to Lucan, enhancing public transport options. The area is accessible via the N4 and is well-served by bus routes through the Bus Connects network. Additionally, the area includes cycling infrastructure like the Western Canals Greenway, which provides scenic and functional routes for cyclists through Griffeen Valley Park and toward Liffey Valley.

Education and Community Facilities: Adamstown has primary and secondary schools, including Adamstown Educate Together and Adamstown Community College, as well as local creches. Recent years have seen investment in community facilities, such as a community centre, playing pitches, and sports facilities like a new astro pitch. Additional parks, such as Airlie Park and Tandy`s Lane Park, contribute to the green spaces in the area.

Retail and Recreation: For shopping, Adamstown hosts `The Crossings` centre, featuring stores like Tesco and Aldi, along with other retail outlets. Larger shopping destinations like Liffey Valley Shopping Centre are also nearby. Adamstown has sports clubs, including soccer, GAA, and cricket, catering to community sports needs, alongside plans to expand local leisure opportunities. The area`s natural environment includes protected spaces like the Liffey Valley and Griffeen Park, designated for conservation and recreational use.

This combination of residential, transport, and community planning makes Adamstown an essential part of South Dublin`s urban development strategy, supporting sustainable growth while enhancing quality of life for residents.
